The tool kinds a session's `before-tool` hooks and rules subscribe to, by how each reaches them: through the
permission seam (the lock makes the agent ask), through the adapter's `_drgnx/before_tool`, or not at all (the
agent runs them without asking). Fixed at the session's start; never faked.

why.description: Why the unhooked kinds are (shown as "not hooked: KINDS (WHY)").

Mode.description: What a message sent while the session works does.

Panel.description:
The agent's `_drgnx/panel` extension: the features it advertised in `initialize` (`context`, `drop`, `pin`,
`compact-preview`, `before-tool`) and its last `_drgnx/context`.

Permission.description: A permission request the agent waits on.

Review.description: A write held for the user's review.

Role.description: A session's role: what its matrix column is.

RpcId.description: A JSON-RPC id, as the agent chose it.

oneOf.description: Waiting on a job it started (no model request until the wake).

Snapshot.description:
What an editor mirrors of a session, everything but its transcript.  A `service` or `agent` caller of
`agents/list` gets only `{id, name, job, task}`.

browser_why.description:
Why a session whose `browser` cell allows the agent browser started without it, and the fix (a host that
cannot give one: no full sandbox tier, Landlock below ABI 9, no browser found).

enforced_why.description: Why the provider's lock is not enforced (shown "not enforced").

handle.description:
Its name, unique in its workspace: the model's short name, numbered from the second agent of that model on
("Opus", "Opus 2").

held_by.description:
Who holds the session's wheel (`user`, from `agents/wheel/take` until the give): the agent stops after its
step and nothing of it is written until the wheel is given back.

hooked.description: Which tool kinds the `before-tool` hooks of its plugin set at start see, and how (none: nothing subscribes).

last_active.description:
The hub's time of its latest update (seconds since the epoch): which identity a display reuses past its
capacity.

monogram.description: The handle's short form for badges ("O", "O2").

ordinal.description:
Its place among its workspace's live agents (1, 2, …; kept for its life): each display's colour and mark come
from it. Absent once it has ended.

paired.description: A chat in a project: whether pair mode is on for it (its edits of your checkout go through the editor).

panel.description:
What its agent's `_drgnx/panel` extension offers, and the context breakdown it sent last (none: the agent
offers nothing; an editor hides the actions).

parent.description: The manager session that started it.

plugins_changed.description:
The plugins that run for the session differ from the ones it started with: abilities are fixed when the agent
starts, so a new set reaches it only through a new session.

queue.description: Messages waiting for the turn to end.

turns.description:
How many turns this hub process has started for the session: an editor that saw the count rise and no `busy`

waiting.description:
A paired chat whose writes of one file were refused twice within a minute: it waits for the user (or asks)
until a write of that file applies.

Waiting.description: The file (and the user's lines in it) a paired chat waits on.

methods.doc: the editor applied a (view, class)'s patch of this version: an acknowledged view's next patch may go
methods.name: view/ack

params.description:
`view/ack`: the editor applied (VIEW, CLASS)'s patch VERSION. For a view whose patches are acknowledged (a
terminal's), the hub holds the next patch until this; a reconnect or a `view/resync` clears what it waits for.
Other views may send it or not.
params.title: ViewAck

methods.doc: the editor shows a view no more: its envs and rows are forgotten (a connection's views end with it)
methods.name: view/close

params.description: `view/close`: the editor shows VIEW no more; the hub forgets its envs and rows.
params.title: ViewClose

methods.doc: how one view looks in one display class (fonts, scale, width, palette), with the editor's epoch: a new epoch makes the next view-patch a reset
methods.name: view/env

params.description:
`view/env`: how VIEW looks in display class CLASS, measured in the view's buffer. EPOCH is the editor's number for
this env (the hub echoes it on every patch); a new epoch makes the next patch a reset.

attach.description:
The first env of a new buffer for this (view, class): a pair the hub already holds for the connection (no
`view/close` came) is dropped and starts again, so the new buffer gets the rows whole.

cell.description: The frame's character cell, `[width, height]` px.

palette.description: `[role, colour]`: the SVG writer's colours, from the theme.

tty_widths.description: `[from, to, width]`: the terminal's character widths that differ from Unicode's.

tz.description: The editor's offset from UTC, `+HHMM` as `%z` prints it (the trail's times); anything else is UTC.

width_px.description: The narrowest live window of the class showing the view, body px.

params.title: ViewEnv

methods.doc: the editor's advances for the glyphs a view-glyphs asked for, [role, char, px] each
methods.name: view/glyphs

params.description: `view/glyphs`: the editor's answer to `view-glyphs`, `[role, char, px]` each.
params.title: ViewGlyphs

methods.doc: the fit guard's measurements of strings that overflowed, [role, string, px] each: the hub fits by them
methods.name: view/measured

params.description: `view/measured`: the fit guard measured these strings wider than the hub fitted them, `[role, string, px]` each.
params.title: ViewMeasured

methods.doc: the editor's rows of a (view, class) are not the hub's: answered by a view-patch reset; with model, its replica of the view's model is not: answered by a view-model reset
methods.name: view/resync

params.description:
`view/resync`: the editor's rows of (VIEW, CLASS) are not what the hub thinks (a patch's base it does not hold, an
image it lacks); VERSION is what it holds. The answer is a `reset`. With MODEL, it is VIEW's model the editor's
replica cannot take (a gap, a hub it has no reset from): the answer is a `view-model` reset, and CLASS is not read.
params.title: ViewResync

methods.doc: the editor's replica needs another window of a list of a view's model, from a position in the whole list: the view's builder sends the model with that window
methods.name: view/window

params.description:
`view/window`: the editor's replica of VIEW's model needs another window of list LIST, starting at FROM (a
position in the whole list; the hub clamps it). The view's builder sends the model with that window, whole
(docs/develop/core.md, "Views": windows); the answer is false when no builder holds such a list.
params.title: ViewWindow
